name: @driftbox/app
description: Driftbox — a drum machine and step sequencer in the browser. Run it with npx @driftbox/app.
author: Louis Emmett
//publishConfig: Scoped packages are RESTRICTED by default, and restricted publishing needs a paid npm plan — so without this the first release fails with a 402 that no dry run catches, because --dry-run never makes the access check. Set here rather than passed as --access public on the command line so that publishing by hand from a laptop cannot differ from publishing from CI.
//engines: A floor, not a support statement: nothing in either package uses an API newer than this. The engine compiles no further than ??= (ES2021), and the app’s bin uses only node: specifiers, ?? and optional chaining. CI builds and tests on 24.

scripts.//icons: Regenerates the manifest icons from public/favicon.svg. Not part of the build — the PNGs are committed; this is what you re-run when the artwork changes.
scripts.//verify:offline: Needs a dist/. Serves it at the root and at /driftbox/, registers the worker, pulls the network and reloads — the only way to test the claim is to make it.
scripts.//check:size: Needs a dist/. Budgets what each page costs to open, and asserts no scene is in either first-load graph.

//: No runtime dependencies, deliberately. What ships is a prebuilt dist/ with everything already bundled into it, and a bin that serves it using nothing but Node built-ins — so `npx @driftbox/app` downloads one small package and runs, instead of resolving React, three and the rest first. That includes @driftbox/engine: it is compiled into the bundle at build time, so listing it as a dependency would make every user install a copy nothing loads.
